note: #2633 asks whether HLSL can be compiled to a relocatable SPIR-V module -- functions exported from one file and imported by another. This predicate measures the IMPORT half, which is the half that is still missing. The symptom of the capability being absent is a DIAGNOSTIC, so the diagnostic text is written in verbatim rather than approximated: SKILL.md step 6 (`_predicate_quotes`) needs the exact string or the invalid-probe classifier scores matching probes differently. Measured wording on main-debug (ab5400907): `repro.hlsl:27:21: error: found undefined function`, exit 0x80004005 (E_FAIL -- an ORDINARY DIAGNOSED ERROR, not a crash; dxc returns E_FAIL for syntax errors too). The text has been unchanged since 04a526945 (2017-11-24, PR #847), which predates every probeable release, so it is stable across the whole scan. It is emitted from SpirvEmitter.cpp:3227 when a call has no callee body. THIS IS NOT AN ABSENCE PREDICATE: it asserts output the compiler had to produce, so it cannot be satisfied for free by a run that failed early, and it cannot be falsified for free by a diagnostic echoing the construct back (the #3092 trap). MEASURED INVARIANT under flags, all still `found undefined function` on main-debug: -fspv-target-env=universal1.5; +-fcgl; +-Vd; -T lib_6_6 (the profile @s-perron's own https://godbolt.org/z/4s8xaEdTK uses); -T lib_6_9. CONTROLS, both captured: control-defined.hlsl is repro.hlsl with `foo` DEFINED and must not match (--expect no-match) -- it proves the predicate is not firing on `lib_6_3 + -spirv + a call`, and doubles as the per-release feature-presence control for `-T lib_6_3 -spirv`; variant-inline-spirv-import.hlsl attempts the [[vk::ext_capability(17)]] / [[vk::ext_decorate_string(41,"foo")]] escape hatch and must still match (--expect match), which is what shows there is no user-level workaround. cmd.txt runs two lines; only line 1 (repro.hlsl) can produce this text. The EXPORT half has its own predicate, match-export.json, with DELIBERATELY OPPOSITE polarity -- read its note before comparing the two histories.
